Critically, `makepkg --printsrcinfo` executes code only in the top-level scope during sourcing, and does NOT run pkgver(), prepare(), build(), or package(). None of the top-level definitions include eval, base64, curl|bash, wget|bash, or other dangerous command patterns. There is no code that would download and execute untrusted payloads or exfiltrate data during this step. The use of double-quoted strings with ${pkgver} variable expansion is standard PKGBUILD practice and does not constitute code execution.
</details>

The package() function does nothing beyond a standard install -Dm755 into $pkgdir/usr/bin. There is no obfuscation, no eval/base64 decoding, no curl|bash patterns, no exfiltration of local data, no execution of downloaded scripts, and no modification of unrelated system files. The maintainer's riseup.net email is a common privacy-preserving choice in the AUR community and is not indicative of malice.
